top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye) is the only proposal where achievement, maturity and credit all hold at once: the magic-wavelength condition is a specific, non-obvious idea with a named originator, and its realisation at 10^-18 through control of blackbody, density and higher-order lattice shifts has been reproduced in several laboratories and species and is already used for redshift and constant-variation tests. Two names are shared by every proposal, so no arbitrary cut is needed. The reservation is that it is an invention plus demonstration rather than a new phenomenon. B001 follows because it is the most mature field, with the experiment-only trio (P005) preferred over the mixed trio (P004) for cleaner credit; P003 is robust as a discovery but young with a real attribution gap; P002 has the strongest science but no agreed rule for the three names; no award is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for the credited laureates of any proposal; my documented collaborations (L'Huillier and the Lund group, Keller at ETH, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not among the credited names on P001-P005.
